Disclosures include last three years’ payout ratios and justification for any deviation from policy.

rcsa.risk: Breach of the dividend payout ratio cap
Declaration of dividend when ineligible
CRAR falling below 15% post-dividend
Failure to obtain board certification on provisioning coverage

title: NBFC – Credit Information Reporting
function: Mandates membership of all Credit Information Companies (CICs) and lays down timelines for furnishing borrower data.
actions: Report borrower data (including retail, SME and co-lending exposures) to all CICs at least monthly, with near-real-time reporting for high-ticket loans.
Establish processes for timely correction of disputes raised by borrowers through CICs.
Protect CIC data by using secure APIs and restricting internal access on a need-to-know basis.
Membership in all four CICs (TransUnion CIBIL, Equifax, Experian, CRIF) is mandatory; data must be furnished at least monthly, and exposures ≥₹5 crore reported to CRILC on a weekly basis.
other: Non-reporting or inaccurate reporting attracts monetary penalties and supervisory action.
Membership fees and data-sharing agreements must be kept current for all CICs.
Borrower consent requirements align with the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act.
controls: Automate daily/weekly bureau file generation with validation for identification fields and repayment data.
Implement dispute management workflows to resolve borrower complaints within 30 days.
Restrict access to bureau data via role-based controls and maintain audit logs.
reporting: Maintain evidence of timely submissions to all CICs and produce during inspections.
Disclose CIC membership status and grievance channels on the NBFC website.
Report systemic errors or data breaches involving CIC information to RBI and impacted customers.
thresholds: Membership in all four CICs (TransUnion CIBIL, Equifax, Experian, CRIF) is mandatory; data must be furnished at least monthly, and exposures ≥₹5 crore reported to CRILC on a weekly basis.
Disputes raised by borrowers must be resolved within 30 days; failure attracts penalties up to ₹1 lakh per day of delay.
Data files must meet ≥98% accuracy score in CIC validation; rejection beyond 2% must be rectified within 7 days.
deep_dive: Data needs to include account status, collateral, days past due and restructuring flags. NBFCs must maintain secure API connections with CICs and restrict access through need-to-know controls plus quarterly user recertification. Negative reporting of guarantors is compulsory once guarantee is invoked, and closed accounts must be updated within 7 days of settlement.

rcsa.risk: Delay or failure to furnish data to all four CICs
Failure to resolve borrower disputes within 30 days
Data accuracy falling below the 98% threshold
Failure to report large exposures to CRILC on a weekly basis

title: NBFC – Know Your Customer
function: Adopts the RBI Master KYC Direction for NBFCs covering CDD, beneficial ownership, V-CIP and record retention.
actions: Perform full CDD at onboarding, including identification of beneficial owners for juridical persons and verification of PAN/Aadhaar as applicable.
Use V-CIP or CKYCR only in line with RBI-prescribed safeguards, video recording quality and geo-tagging requirements.
Monitor transactions for suspicious patterns, file STRs/CTRs with FIU-IND and maintain KYC records for at least ten years after relationship ends.
Small accounts opened with simplified KYC capped at ₹1 lakh aggregate credit in a year and ₹50,000 balance at any time; transactions beyond these require full KYC.
other: Risk-based periodic KYC update cycles must be defined (high, medium, low risk).
Non-face-to-face onboarding requires additional verification such as OTP-based e-KYC plus liveliness checks.
Customer due diligence obligations apply equally to walk-in customers of NBFC agents.
controls: Adopt risk-based customer acceptance policies with enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk sectors.
Ensure V-CIP journeys incorporate liveness detection, geo-tagging and video recording retention.
Periodic KYC refresh cycles triggered automatically with alerts to branches and BCs.
reporting: File STRs/CTRs to FIU-IND through FINnet portal and maintain acknowledgement numbers.
Report significant KYC/AML breaches or regulatory penalties to the board and RBI promptly.
Maintain CKYCR upload evidence and respond to regulator queries on record-keeping within stipulated time.
thresholds: Small accounts opened with simplified KYC capped at ₹1 lakh aggregate credit in a year and ₹50,000 balance at any time; transactions beyond these require full KYC.
Periodic KYC updates: every 2 years for high-risk, 8 years for medium-risk, 10 years for low-risk customers.
V-CIP sessions must have minimum 12 fps video quality, geo-tagging of customer location, and concurrent audit sampling of at least 10% of sessions.
deep_dive: Beneficial ownership thresholds: 10% for companies and 15% for partnership/LLP. Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC permitted only for bank-mandated categories; NBFCs must rely on CKYCR for central storage. Suspicious transactions (STRs) and Cash Transaction Reports (CTRs) must hit FIU-IND via FINnet within 7 working days of detection, and records must be kept for 10 years after exit.

rcsa.risk: Breach of small account limits
Failure to conduct periodic KYC updates as per risk categorization
Non-compliance with V-CIP quality and audit requirements
Delay in filing of STRs/CTRs with FIU-IND

title: NBFC – Credit Cards: Issuance & Conduct
function: Extends the card issuance, billing, co-branding and recovery standards to NBFCs authorised to issue credit cards.
actions: Obtain specific RBI approval before issuing cards, ensure underwriting is independent of sponsors and avoid unsolicited cards or upgrades.
Send statements with minimum 14 days for payment, avoid negative amortisation, and allow no-cost EMI only when merchant discount fully offsets interest.
Disclose all fees, interest reset clauses and conversion charges upfront; maintain 24x7 dispute redress and chargeback timelines.
Billing cycle must allow minimum 14-day grace period; finance charges cannot exceed those disclosed at origination and must be capped per board policy (industry median ~3.5% per month).
other: Co-branded arrangements require NBFC control over KYC, underwriting and collections.
Recovery agents must follow RBI's conduct rules and operate only between permitted hours.
Closure requests must be honoured within seven working days, failing which penalties apply.
controls: Calibrate underwriting scorecards distinct from parent bank/NBFC lending rules and monitor vintage performance.
Run automated scripts to capture customer consent for add-on products, EMI conversions and third-party offers.
Implement chargeback governance with defined TATs, root-cause analysis and restitution policies.
reporting: Provide RBI with portfolio-level data on sourcing channels, delinquencies, interest waivers and fee income.
Disclose co-branding partners, outsourcing arrangements and major incidents in the annual statement.
Offer customers downloadable statements, MITC (Most Important Terms & Conditions) and closure acknowledgements.
thresholds: Billing cycle must allow minimum 14-day grace period; finance charges cannot exceed those disclosed at origination and must be capped per board policy (industry median ~3.5% per month).
Card closure requests must be honoured within 7 working days; failure entails ₹500 per day compensation.
Co-branded partnerships require the NBFC to hold at least 51% control over KYC, underwriting and collections.
deep_dive: Explicit consent is required for increasing credit limits or converting purchases into EMI—silence cannot be treated as consent. Chargebacks must be resolved within 30 days (120 days for cross-border). Any telemarketing/collection agency must confine calls between 8 a.m. and 7 p.m.; breach invites penalties and blacklisting. Card data storage must comply with PCI-DSS, and tokenisation is mandatory for online use.

rcsa.risk: Failure to provide a minimum 14-day grace period
Failure to close cards within 7 working days
Lack of 51% control in co-branded partnerships
Failure to obtain explicit consent for limit increases or EMI conversions

title: NBFC – Responsible Business Conduct
function: Consolidates fair lending, transparency, suitability and grievance redress norms for all customer interfaces.
actions: Adopt an updated Fair Practices Code covering product design, marketing communication, staff incentives and treatment of vulnerable customers.
Publish key fact statements for every retail loan, capturing APR, fees, cooling-off rights and contact points.
Track complaint ageing, root cause and compensation metrics via board-level Service Quality Committees.
Key Fact Statements must be issued for all retail loans above ₹5,000 with APR, fees and recovery timelines; customers receive a 3-day cooling-off period for digital loans.
other: Digital lending partners must display NBFC identity and comply with consent artefact rules.
Field recovery staff must carry authorisation letters and audio-record visits when feasible.
NBFCs must participate in RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme and display details prominently.
controls: Embed Fair Practices Code elements into LOS/LMS so communications auto-populate key fact data.
Use speech analytics / mystery shopping to verify adherence to sales and recovery scripts.
Maintain vulnerability-sensitive policies for senior citizens, MSMEs and digitally excluded customers.
reporting: Run Service Quality dashboards capturing TATs, complaint resolution and compensation numbers for the board.
Disclose grievance redress statistics, ombudsman awards and compensation paid annually.
Report serious conduct breaches to RBI within 15 days and document remedial coaching or disciplinary action.
thresholds: Key Fact Statements must be issued for all retail loans above ₹5,000 with APR, fees and recovery timelines; customers receive a 3-day cooling-off period for digital loans.
Complaints acknowledged within 48 hours and resolved within 30 days; unresolved cases automatically escalate to the Internal Ombudsman.
Field recovery visits require geo-tagging and audio recording when ticket size exceeds ₹50,000.
deep_dive: Fair Practices Codes must cover product suitability assessments, incentive alignment and prohibition of harassment. NBFCs must also participate in RBI’s CMS (Complaint Management System) and integrate real-time feedback loops. Refunds for wrongful debits must occur within 7 days, and any systemic issue demands board-reviewed root cause analysis.

rcsa.risk: Failure to issue KFS for all eligible loans
Failure to resolve complaints within 30 days
Failure to record field recovery visits for large ticket sizes
Outdated or non-compliant Fair Practices Code

title: NBFC – Voluntary Amalgamation
function: Sets the approval process and prudential filters for amalgamation or merger of two NBFCs.
actions: Obtain RBI no-objection before filing any scheme with NCLT; application must include swap ratios, financials, and post-merger capital plan.
Ensure combined entity meets NOF, SBR layer capital and governance requirements on the effective date.
Communicate with customers and creditors about the merger and honour all contractual obligations seamlessly.
Two independent valuers must certify the share swap ratio; fairness opinion from SEBI-registered merchant banker compulsory for listed NBFCs.
other: RBI may impose conditions such as branch rationalisation, promoter dilution or staggered integration.
All regulatory approvals from other sectoral regulators must be annexed before final sanction.
If merger results in change of control, the acquisition rules apply simultaneously.
controls: Set up integration management offices covering credit, IT, HR and governance streams with RBI-observed milestones.
Track synergy assumptions versus actuals and escalate deviations to the board.
Ensure customer communications, account numbers and repayment instructions transition seamlessly.
reporting: Submit periodic progress reports to RBI on merger integration, capital position and compliance with conditions.
File revised CoR, shareholding patterns and branch rationalisation plans post-merger.
Disclose scheme highlights, swap ratios and expected benefits to investors and customers.
thresholds: Two independent valuers must certify the share swap ratio; fairness opinion from SEBI-registered merchant banker compulsory for listed NBFCs.
Combined entity must have CRAR ≥15%, Tier I ≥10% and NOF above the regulatory minimum on the appointed date.
All creditors and depositors must be given a 30-day public notice; objections to RBI/NCLT must be disclosed in the petition.
deep_dive: Schemes require RBI ‘no objection’ before filing with NCLT. Integration plans must cover IT migration, HR harmonisation and risk management conversions with timelines; RBI can impose conditions like promoter dilution or branch rationalisation. Post-merger, fresh certificates of registration and new CoR numbers are issued, and all agreements with lenders must be re-signed.

rcsa.risk: Failure to obtain two independent valuations for the share swap ratio
Failure to meet post-merger prudential norms
Failure to provide 30-day public notice to creditors
Failure to obtain RBI no-objection before filing with NCLT

title: NBFC – Miscellaneous
function: Captures residual instructions such as prohibitions on offering demand deposits, guidelines on gifts/incentives, audit requirements and supervisory powers.
actions: Do not issue bearer instruments, virtual accounts without KYC or any deposit-like product not expressly permitted.
Maintain statutory auditors' independence, rotate partners as per RBI timelines and submit fraud monitoring returns promptly.
Respond to RBI inspection findings within mandated timelines and implement corrective action tracking.
Section 45IC requires transfer of at least 20% of net profit to the statutory reserve every year until it equals the paid-up capital.
other: Monetary penalties for each contravention can extend up to INR 1 crore plus continuing penalties.
RBI may exempt specific provisions or extend compliance dates in public interest but expects detailed justification.
Directions supplement, and where necessary override, sectoral laws like Factoring Regulation Act or NHB Act.
controls: Maintain a living compliance inventory listing every circular, master direction and due date mapped to owners.
Conduct quarterly self-assessments on prohibited activities (demand deposits, trading) and document evidence.
Implement whistle-blower and fraud monitoring frameworks aligned with RBI instructions.
reporting: File fraud monitoring returns (FMR) and submission on cyber incidents as required.
Respond to supervisory letters with action-taken reports and evidence closures within agreed timelines.
Disclose penalties, show-cause notices and remediation plans in annual reports when mandated.
thresholds: Section 45IC requires transfer of at least 20% of net profit to the statutory reserve every year until it equals the paid-up capital.
Penalties for contravention under RBI Act can go up to ₹1 crore plus ₹1 lakh per day for continuing offences.
Any gift or incentive scheme for loan sourcing must cap individual payouts at ₹5,000 per customer to avoid inducement breaches.
deep_dive: The catch-all direction covers prohibition on offering demand deposits, guidance on rounding off transactions, restrictions on use of the word ‘bank’, and instructions on reporting frauds via the FMR platform. It also spells out legal-entity identifier adoption timelines, disaster-recovery expectations and dispensation procedures for temporary hardship. Compliance officers must maintain a living inventory of all circulars with owner names and due dates.

rcsa.risk: Failure to transfer 20% of net profit to the statutory reserve
Engaging in prohibited activities like offering demand deposits
Delay or failure to report frauds via the FMR platform
Incomplete or outdated compliance inventory
